articles.title: Michael Bloomberg was fired from a Wall Street bank after 15 years. He used his $10 million payout to build a $109 billion fortune and has given away $25.4 billion
articles.summary: US News: Michael Bloomberg was 39 when his 15-year career at Wall Street investment bank Salomon Brothers came to an end in 1981. A general partner at the firm.
articles.body: Michael Bloomberg was 39 when his 15-year career at Wall Street investment bank Salomon Brothers came to an end in 1981. A general partner at the firm, Bloomberg left as Salomon was being acquired by Phibro Corporation and received about $10 million for his stake. Rather than use the money to retire or join another Wall Street firm, he put it towards an idea shaped by his years in finance. Bloomberg believed financial professionals needed faster and more efficient access to market information, and he set out to build a company around that idea. The venture became Bloomberg LP and eventually grew into a global financial information and media company. Forbes now estimates Bloomberg's fortune at about $109.4 billion and his lifetime charitable giving at $25.4 billion.Michael Bloomberg was fired after 15 years at Salomon BrothersBloomberg joined Salomon Brothers in 1966 after graduating from Johns Hopkins University and Harvard Business School. He began in an entry-level position and worked his way up through the investment bank, eventually becoming a general partner. He also took responsibility for the firm's information systems, giving him an early understanding of how technology could change the way financial professionals accessed and processed market data. In 1981, Salomon Brothers was acquired by Phibro Corporation, and Bloomberg was among the partners who left the firm. Bloomberg has described the event as being fired from the only full-time job he had known. His departure ended a 15-year Wall Street career, but it also gave him the financial resources and independence to pursue his own business idea.Bloomberg used his $10 million payout to start a companyWhen Bloomberg left Salomon Brothers, he received roughly $10 million for his partnership stake. The money became the financial foundation for his next venture. Instead of looking for another position in finance, he founded Innovative Market Systems in 1981 with former Salomon colleagues Thomas Secunda, Duncan MacMillan and Charles Zegar. The company's objective was to provide financial professionals with better access to market information through technology. Bloomberg had seen at Salomon how valuable timely financial data could be, as well as how difficult it could be to gather information from multiple sources. His new company aimed to put data, analytics and financial information directly in front of users through computer terminals.The Bloomberg Terminal became the company's breakthroughThe company secured an important early customer when Merrill Lynch agreed to purchase Bloomberg's financial information terminals. Merrill Lynch eventually ordered 20 terminals and invested $30 million in the company for a 30% stake. The system developed into the Bloomberg Terminal, which combined real-time financial data, analytics, news and communications in a single platform. The terminal gave traders and other financial professionals a faster way to access information and analyse markets. As more financial institutions adopted the technology, Bloomberg LP grew from a small start-up into a major financial information business. The terminal remains one of the company's best-known products and became the foundation for Bloomberg's expansion into other areas.Bloomberg expanded into news and mediaBloomberg's business eventually moved beyond financial terminals. The company launched Bloomberg Business News in 1990, later known as Bloomberg News, creating a newsroom focused heavily on financial and business reporting. Bloomberg LP subsequently expanded into television, radio, magazines and digital media. The combination of financial data, technology and journalism became a defining feature of the company. Bloomberg's business model also allowed the company to build a large recurring-revenue operation serving financial institutions around the world. Over time, Bloomberg LP became a global financial information and media company, while Bloomberg retained a substantial ownership stake.Bloomberg's fortune reached more than $109 billionBloomberg's wealth is closely tied to his ownership of Bloomberg LP. Forbes estimates that he owns about 88% of the privately held company. Forbes' current real-time estimate puts his net worth at approximately $109.4 billion, although the figure can change as valuations and other financial factors change. His fortune therefore represents the estimated value of his assets and business interests rather than $109 billion held as cash. The Bloomberg Terminal and the company's broader financial information operations have been central to creating and sustaining that wealth over the decades since he left Salomon Brothers.Bloomberg has given away $25.4 billionBloomberg has also become one of America's largest individual philanthropists. Through Bloomberg Philanthropies and other charitable giving, he has directed billions of dollars towards public health, education, climate and environmental initiatives, arts and culture, and efforts to improve cities and government. Forbes estimates that Bloomberg's lifetime charitable giving reached $25.4 billion by the end of 2025. The figure includes billions committed to organisations and initiatives across several fields, making philanthropy a major part of how Bloomberg has used his wealth.Johns Hopkins received billions in Bloomberg donationsEducation has been one of the largest beneficiaries of Bloomberg's philanthropy. In 2018, Bloomberg announced a $1.8 billion gift to Johns Hopkins University, his alma mater, to support financial aid and help the university maintain need-blind admissions. He later pledged another $1 billion to the university in 2024 to support financial aid for medical students. His total giving to Johns Hopkins has consequently reached more than $3.5 billion, according to Forbes. Bloomberg has also committed hundreds of millions of dollars to strengthen historically Black medical schools and support other educational initiatives.His philanthropy extends beyond educationBloomberg's charitable work covers a broad range of issues. Bloomberg Philanthropies supports programmes focused on reducing tobacco use, improving public health, tackling climate change, strengthening cities and local governments, expanding educational opportunities and supporting arts organisations. His climate giving has included major commitments to the transition away from coal and efforts to accelerate clean energy. He has also supported initiatives addressing gun violence and other public-health challenges. Bloomberg's approach has often involved combining large financial commitments with long-term programmes designed to influence policy and institutions.A Wall Street setback became the beginning of a new fortuneBloomberg's journey from Salomon Brothers to one of the world's richest people began with an unexpected career setback. At 39, after 15 years on Wall Street, he left the firm with about $10 million and chose to build a financial technology company rather than return to another investment bank. The idea eventually became Bloomberg LP, transforming how financial professionals accessed market information and creating the foundation of his fortune. More than four decades later, Forbes estimates that Bloomberg is worth about $109.4 billion and has given away $25.4 billion during his lifetime. What began as the end of a Wall Street career ultimately became the starting point for one of the world's largest financial information businesses and one of America's biggest philanthropic fortunes.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: How WhatsApp messages and calls led investigators to former USCIS official in alleged $960,000 American citizenship bribery scam
articles.summary: Tech News News: Thousands of WhatsApp messages and hundreds of phone calls helped investigators uncover an alleged bribery scheme involving a former senior U.S. Citiz.
articles.body: Thousands of WhatsApp messages and hundreds of phone calls helped investigators uncover an alleged bribery scheme involving a former senior U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) official, prosecutors say. Ex-USCIS official Lukman Owolabi Ganiyu and his alleged financial accomplice, Adeniyi Akeem Somoye, have been charged over a scheme in which they allegedly accepted nearly $960,000 to manipulate and speed up immigration benefit applications, including citizenship cases.As per a Fox News report, the two men were arrested on federal charges of conspiracy to receive illegal gratuities by a public official, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas. Prosecutors allege the scheme operated from December 2019 through March 2026 and involved applicants paying money in exchange for special treatment.How WhatsApp messages helped investigators trace alleged scamA key part of the investigation was the pair's digital communication with applicants. Investigators found thousands of WhatsApp messages and hundreds of calls between Ganiyu, Somoye and people whose immigration applications they handled, according to prosecutors.The communications allegedly showed repeated contact between the two men and applicants involved in the immigration cases. Prosecutors allege the pair used these contacts as part of a system in which applicants paid for their cases to be pushed through the immigration process, the report states.Former USCIS official allegedly fast-tracked citizenship casesAccording to the allegations, Ganiyu used his position at USCIS to bypass normal procedures for applicants who paid bribes. Prosecutors say some applications were moved forward without key steps such as criminal background checks, interviews, standard USCIS processing procedures and other reviews.Ganiyu allegedly changed information in the USCIS system to speed up applications. Prosecutors also allege that he moved cases from USCIS field offices in Minneapolis, Charlotte and Houston so that he could approve them himself, bypassing local supervisors.The complaint further alleges that Ganiyu fast-tracked Somoye's citizenship application before approving residency applications for Somoye's wife and child.Prosecutors say nearly $960,000 was paidCourt documents cited in the report say Ganiyu received about $671,438 from citizenship applicants through Zelle and Cash App. He also allegedly received $287,830 through cash deposits that prosecutors say were intended to hide the source of the money.Somoye allegedly acted as a financial intermediary. Prosecutors say he handled about $1.7 million in transfers involving applicants through bank accounts, Zelle and Cash App, while allegedly keeping part of the money. He also allegedly deposited $449,010 in cash. The complaint says Ganiyu and Somoye frequently exchanged money "back and forth" with applicants.According to prosecutors, most of the citizenship applications handled by the pair involved applicants from African countries. The allegations cover a period of more than six years, from December 2019 until March 2026.Ganiyu resigned from USCIS in March, citing "personal reasons," according to the report. He was arrested several months later.Get the latest technology news and updates. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: Mississippi teen Madalyn Sullivan wrote an autism-acceptance book inspired by her sister and sent it to libraries in all 82 counties; she has now finished second at Miss America’s Teen
articles.summary: US News: Madalyn Sullivan, Miss Mississippi’s Teen and an Oxford native, has finished as first runner-up at Miss America’s Teen. The high school student reache.
articles.body: Madalyn Sullivan, Miss Mississippi’s Teen and an Oxford native, has finished as first runner-up at Miss America’s Teen. The high school student reached the national stage after years of advocating for autism acceptance, inspired by her sister, and using that experience to create Millie’s Mission.Sullivan competed through a week of events before the final competition. According to Super Talk FM's report, her schedule included interviews, a talent portion, preliminary competitions and public appearances. The final was held at the Kravis Center for the Performing Arts, where Miss Utah’s Teen Elle Anderson was crowned Miss America’s Teen 2027.Sullivan finished second among the five finalists. Anderson took the title, followed by Sullivan, Miss South Carolina’s Teen Logan Wells, Miss Texas’ Teen Zoe Zogleman and Miss Minnesota’s Teen Natalia Yurecko.Sullivan received a $9,000 scholarship for finishing as first runner-up. Earlier in the week, she won the Evening Wear Preliminary competition, earning another $1,500 scholarship.For Sullivan, however, the pageant is only one part of the work she has been doing. Away from the stage, the Oxford High School student has been using her own family experience to promote autism acceptance through an initiative called Millie’s Mission.A mission inspired by her sisterSullivan’s interest in autism advocacy began with her younger sister. She said her sister was diagnosed with autism when she was 2, while Sullivan was 5 years old.“My sister was diagnosed with autism when she was 2, and I was 5 at the time, and since then I have tried to be one of her biggest advocates,” Sullivan said, as quoted by WAPT.Sullivan said she grew up reading to her sister’s classroom about autism. That experience eventually led her to create something of her own that could be shared with children and families.She co-authored a children’s book called “Meet Millie”. The book was created as part of Millie’s Mission, the initiative she founded to promote autism acceptance and encourage a more inclusive society for people with autism.Sullivan eventually took the book across Mississippi. She said “Meet Millie” is available on Amazon and that she donated copies to public libraries in all 82 counties in the state.Reading the book with her sisterThe project has also given Sullivan a way to work alongside the sister who inspired it. Sullivan said her sister joins her when she reads “Meet Millie” and that the two have fun during those sessions.For Sullivan, the book is connected directly to the larger purpose of Millie’s Mission. “The goal of Millie's Mission is to create a more inclusive society for those with autism,” she said.As Miss Mississippi’s Teen, Sullivan had planned to use her year-long platform to encourage communities to support families affected by autism.Sullivan is also active outside her advocacy and pageant work. She is an Oxford High School student and takes part in several school activities. She is a member of the dance team, runs cross country, sings in the choir and participates in the theatre programme.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Panchayat 5’ release date: When and where to watch the series as Deepak Kumar Mishra reveals when Jitendra Kumar starrer show could stream
articles.summary: News News: ‘Panchayat’ is returning for its fifth season, with Jitendra Kumar reprising his popular role as Abhishek Tripathi. The Prime Video series continues t.
articles.body: ‘Panchayat’ is returning for its fifth season, with Jitendra Kumar reprising his popular role as Abhishek Tripathi. The Prime Video series continues to be among the most-awaited OTT shows, thanks to its sharply written characters, understated humour and grounded portrayal of life in Phulera. While the makers are yet to announce an official release date, director Deepak Kumar Mishra has offered a fresh update on the upcoming season and indicated when viewers can expect it to arrive.‘Panchayat 5’ editing is underwaySpeaking to India Today, Deepak Kumar Mishra revealed that work on the fifth season is currently progressing in the post-production stage. The director said, “The editing process is currently underway. The exact release date has not been finalised yet. It could be around October or November.”Mishra also shared details about the story ahead, suggesting that the new season will focus on how the characters deal with the aftermath of the Phulera elections. He explained, “Sabki zindagi aage badhegi. Elections toh ho gaye. Pradhan Ji haar gaye. But uske aage zindagi unki kaise aage badh rahi hai, baaki characters ki zindagi aage kaise badh rahi hai. Ek haara hua Pradhan kaise ab gaon mein chalta hai, phirta hai, kya karta hai (Everyone's lives will move forward. The elections are over. Pradhan Ji has lost. But the story will explore how his life moves forward after that, and how the lives of the other characters progress as well. How does a Pradhan who has lost an election move around the village now? What does he do)?”Will ‘Panchayat 5’ be the final season?With the fifth season following the conclusion of the Phulera elections, fans have naturally been wondering whether the upcoming instalment could mark the end of the beloved series. However, Mishra has dismissed those speculations.When asked if ‘Panchayat 5’ could bring the show to a close, the director gave a brief response: “Nahi, aisa kuch nahi hai (No, it's nothing like that).”His comment indicates that the story of Abhishek, Pradhan Ji and the other residents of Phulera is not necessarily approaching its conclusion with the fifth season.‘Panchayat 5’ cast and show backgroundProduced by The Viral Fever (TVF) and directed by Deepak Kumar Mishra, ‘Panchayat’ premiered in 2020 and quickly developed a strong following for its slice-of-life storytelling and memorable ensemble.The series follows Abhishek Tripathi, played by Jitendra Kumar, a postgraduate who takes up a job as secretary of the gram panchayat in the fictional village of Phulera. His attempts to navigate village politics, personal relationships and everyday challenges form the heart of the show.The ensemble cast includes Neena Gupta, Raghubir Yadav, Chandan Roy, Faisal Malik, Sanvikaa, Durgesh Kumar, Ashok Pathak, Sunita Rajwar and Pankaj Jha in pivotal roles. With editing currently underway and October-November being discussed as a possible release window, fans will have to wait for an official announcement before the exact ‘Panchayat 5’ premiere date is confirmed.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Actor-turned-politician Kangana Ranaut said "character assassination of women" must stop, calling on society to examine its attitude towards women. She said women, particularly those in positions of power and authority, are often targeted through attacks on their character in an attempt to undermine them."We all know that this is not restricted to India alone and is prevalent worldwide that character of working women, successful women, actors, politicians, women at the position of power and authority is targeted to bring her down," Ranaut told reporters after chairing the District Development Coordination and Monitoring meeting at Kullu on Monday.The BJP MP's remarks came when she was asked about Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay's recent speech in which he warned against personal attacks, double-meaning insults and derogatory remarks targeting women.Ranaut, who played former Tamil Nadu chief minister J Jayalalithaa in the 2021 biopic Thalaivii, referred to the alleged humiliation Jayalalithaa faced in the Tamil Nadu Assembly."In Tamil Nadu, we have seen that a very renowned actress was targeted for her relations," she said, adding that relations are from both sides but only the woman is targeted for abuse, "cheer haran" (disrobing) and character assassination."We as a society should look into our self that how do we look at women and do we really respect them or not,” she added.Vijay, in his speech in the Tamil Nadu Assembly, criticised derogatory political remarks against women and invoked the alleged abuse and humiliation faced by Jayalalithaa during the 1989 Assembly episode.His remarks came amid a recent controversy over comments attributed to DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin concerning actor Trisha, an issue whose interpretation has been disputed by the DMK.The Assembly also witnessed ruckus on Tuesday after the DMK objected to Vijay's remarks and demanded that references based on Enforcement Directorate documents be expunged from the records.Opposition MLAs raised slogans and were evicted from the House.The confrontation began after Vijay, while speaking on the Home Department articles.title: AI boom has put several of the biggest American universities are under 'physical threat', George Washington University’s sale of its Virginia campus is an example
articles.summary: Tech News News: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is creating a new pressure point for American universities. This comes as demand for data centers increases the value of .
articles.body: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is creating a new pressure point for American universities. This comes as demand for data centers increases the value of large properties with access to electricity, water and fiber infrastructure. American universities that have traditionally used such land for classrooms, laboratories and research facilities are increasingly competing with AI infrastructure projects, creating what former George Washington University professor Ellen Scully-Russ described as “a physical threat” to higher education resources.​The George Washington (GW) University’s sale of its roughly 120-acre Virginia Science and Technology Campus in Ashburn, Virginia, to Amazon Data Services for $427 million is one example of this shift. “Universities are large landholders, and there is a land grab going on with the data centers these days,” Scully-Russ told Fortune. The campus is located in Loudoun County, part of Northern Virginia’s “Data Center Alley”, a major concentration of data centers.George Washington University’s $427 million campus sale for AI data center​GW University announced the sale in February but initially did not identify the buyer or disclose the price, citing confidentiality provisions. Amazon Data Services was later identified as the buyer, paying $427 million for the property.The university said the transaction would strengthen its long-term financial position. GW can continue using the campus for up to five years while it determines how to relocate the programmes and offices operating there. A significant portion of the proceeds will be placed into a new endowment, while eligible faculty and staff will receive one-time payments of $2,500 for benefits-eligible full-time faculty and $1,250 for eligible part-time faculty.The sale came as GW faces financial pressures linked to changes in federal research funding, international student policies and broader challenges affecting higher education. The university has said the transaction will support its finances and allow it to invest in its academic mission.Scully-Russ, who joined GW in 2009 to teach and lead a programme at the Virginia campus, said the property struggled to become a central part of the university’s strategy, despite having newer facilities than some at its Washington, DC, campus.​“It never really got any legs, in my opinion,” she said.She also described a gradual reduction in resources at the campus over several years, including faculty departures that were not replaced and the eventual elimination of teaching assistants because of budget constraints. She said faculty and students were not informed in advance that the university was considering selling the property.“There was no transparency,” she told Fortune. “The faculty, the student body, as far as I know, were not even aware that there was a discussion about selling to anybody, let alone to Amazon.”GW held town halls after the sale was announced to discuss the transition of programmes, faculty and staff from the campus. Scully-Russ questioned the timing of that consultation.“It’s kind of like, do you really care?” she said. “Did you care what I thought before you made this decision? Did you care to let me know that this was in the works?”​However, the George Washington University did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Scully-Russ also raised concerns about universities using land for AI infrastructure while federal funding and other financial pressures affect higher education.“We’re chipping away at our higher ed resources to make room for this technology to expand without any accountability,” she told Fortune, “or any other kind of thoughtful progression, which is really a concern for me.”She also questioned the long-term demand for large AI infrastructure projects.​“I think it’s just a short-term bubble,” she said. “We’re just one technological leap away from having those huge ugly buildings being obsolete. Then what happens?”​University of Michigan builds $1.25 billion AI computing centre​The University of Michigan is taking a different approach to AI infrastructure through a planned $1.25 billion high-performance computing and research centre in Ypsilanti Township.​Developed with Los Alamos National Laboratory, the project is intended to support research in areas including medicine, materials science, clean energy, engineering, and national security. The university describes the facility as a computing centre rather than a commercial data center and says it will support “applying AI and high-performance computing.”The university has acquired land for the project. In 2024, its Board of Regents approved purchases of 19.82 acres and 6.03 acres in Ypsilanti Township for a future computing centre. In 2025, it received authorisation to purchase about 124.7 acres on Textile Road for the facility.The university has also distinguished the project from commercial data centers, saying the facility will focus on scientific research rather than cloud computing, streaming, e-commerce and other consumer or business applications.The planned facility is expected to require about 50 megawatts of power initially, eventually reaching 100 megawatts, according to a university report.The project has faced opposition from local residents and officials. The Ypsilanti Township Board of Trustees unanimously passed a resolution opposing the proposed computational research facility, “declaring strong and unequivocal opposition.”​Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Brahmos shy, Pakistan claims to have procured new weapons
articles.summary: News News: The Pakistani Air Force (PAF) claims to have procured newer weapon types that it hopes will help defend against the type of aerial attacks that the In.
articles.body: The Pakistani Air Force (PAF) claims to have procured newer weapon types that it hopes will help defend against the type of aerial attacks that the Indian Air Force unleashed on air bases across Pakistan during Operation SindoorIndian attacks on Pakistani air defences destroyed the radars of Pakistan's Chinese-origin HQ-16 Surface to Air Missile (SAM) system. On defence of Pakistan Day, commemorating the 1965 war (a conflict that the country ended up losing), the PAF revealed close-in air defence equipment that it hopes will shield its air bases in case a conflict does flare up in the future.The new equipment showcased by the Pakistanis is of both Chinese and Turkish origin, according to Bloomberg. The first of these systems is the HQ-17A system, which is derived by the Chinese from the Russian Tor-M1 system. Like the Russian Tor, the HQ-17 is an all-weather, low-to medium-altitude, short-range surface-to-air missile system that is designed to destroy airplanes, helicopters, cruise missiles and unmanned aerial vehicles. The system can take out targets up to a range of up to 20km and altitude of lower than 35,000 feet. Many stand-off weapons, both currently in use and underdevelopment by the air force, can target a system protected by this weapon from a much greater distance.A supersonic missile, such as the terrain hugging Brahmos that travels at Mach 3 will not be visible to the radar of this weapon till the last few seconds, thus reducing the effectiveness of the HQ-17. India is also developing the Rudram series of Anti-Radiation Missiles (ARM), this family of missiles are designed to destroy air defence radars from much outside the ranges of the weapon firing envelope of current Pakistani air defence systems. These missiles are designed to destroy the radar array of the air defence system. Apart from Pakistan, Turkey and Serbia are in possession of this air defence system.Another air defence weapon procured by the Pakistanis in the recent past and showcased now is a Turkish origin gun based close in weapon system called the KORKUT is a all-weather-capable 35 mm self-propelled anti-aircraft gun (SPAAG) developed by Aselsan. This system is designed around two Swiss developed 35mm guns which have a range of 4km. The Pakistanis already operate the Swiss made weapon system and in terms of ammunition already have the logistics set-up for this weapon. The weapon is expected to give thew Pakistanis similar type of protection as provided by India's L-70 guns, especially against drones and swarm drones.These weapons are expected to provide key Pakistani air force assets some protection against at least some of the weapons that can be employed in a conflict. They could also add an additional layer of air defences when deployed. Pakistan had also deployed air defence weapons during Operation Sindoor, but India's weapons still found their mark. This was achieved due to careful weapon selection and tactics, blunting Pakistan's perceived edge in the domain.In response to many of Pakistan's failed attacks on key Indian locations, which also included the use of ballistic weapons, the Indian Air Force struck back hitting key air bases, air defence sites and early warning radar sites across the length a of Pakistan from Nur Khan air base in the north to Malir Cantt in Karachi in the south.

articles.title: In Japan, local authorities have installed signs warning drivers that cats may suddenly dash into the road, using playful illustrations to make the danger memorable
articles.summary: US News: An unusual road-safety idea in Japan is turning an everyday danger into something drivers are unlikely to forget. In parts of the country, signs featu.
articles.body: An unusual road-safety idea in Japan is turning an everyday danger into something drivers are unlikely to forget. In parts of the country, signs featuring cats warn motorists that an animal could suddenly run into the road. Some of the designs are deliberately playful, using striking cat illustrations rather than conventional wildlife-warning imagery. The idea is rooted in a genuine road-safety concern. Cats can suddenly enter roads while chasing birds or insects, and their sensitivity to noise and light can sometimes cause them to freeze when confronted by a vehicle. Organisations and local authorities have therefore used visual warnings to encourage motorists to slow down and stay alert. The approach has also been adapted for wildlife conservation, including efforts to protect Japan's endangered Tsushima leopard cat from road traffic.Japan installs playful signs to warn drivers about catsOne of the most distinctive examples came from Yellow Hat, a Japanese automotive retailer that launched a road-safety campaign focused specifically on reducing cat traffic accidents. As part of the campaign, the company created a cat warning sign designed to catch drivers' attention and remind them that cats can suddenly enter the road. The design was developed with supervision from a Kyoto University animal psychology research team specialising in companion-animal behaviour. Rather than relying on a standard warning image, the sign attempted to recreate the expression and posture of a cat about to dash into the road. Yellow Hat said the aim was to create a warning that would be particularly effective at attracting attention. The campaign was launched around Cat Day in February 2022, with a sign installed near a school in Tokyo's Shibuya area.The playful designs are based on a real danger for catsBehind the amusing appearance of these signs is a serious problem. Yellow Hat explained that cats can run into roads because of their natural hunting behaviour, particularly when they chase birds or insects. The company also highlighted another difficulty. Cats are highly sensitive to sounds and light, and when confronted by a vehicle they can sometimes become unable to move instead of escaping from the road. That combination can create dangerous situations for both animals and motorists. The campaign therefore encouraged drivers to pay attention to cats while driving and to approach areas where animals may be present with greater care. The unusual artwork was intended to make the warning stand out rather than disappear among the many conventional signs motorists encounter on roads.Tsushima uses warning signs to protect an endangered wild catThe same basic idea becomes even more important on Tsushima, an island in southwestern Japan that is home to the critically endangered Tsushima leopard cat. Japan's Environment Ministry has repeatedly used warning signs and other measures to reduce vehicle collisions involving the species. The Tsushima Wildlife Conservation Center has installed warning boards near areas where leopard cats are known to occur or where previous accidents have happened. In one documented effort, authorities and local partners installed signs around an area with a history of leopard-cat traffic accidents, including signs designed to reflect vehicle headlights at night. Drivers are encouraged to slow down and remain alert, particularly because the animals are active around roads and can suddenly appear in the path of vehicles.Japan combines warning signs with other wildlife protection measuresThe signs are only one part of a broader strategy. On Tsushima, conservation authorities have also used speed warnings, road markings, fencing, under-road passages and other measures intended to reduce the likelihood of animals entering traffic. The Environment Ministry says road accidents remain one of the most serious threats facing the Tsushima leopard cat, whose population is estimated at around 100 individuals. Historical records have documented numerous traffic-related deaths, while officials continue to run awareness campaigns and monitor accident hotspots. In 2024, the Environment Ministry also conducted a road-safety campaign after a leopard cat was killed during the daytime, highlighting that drivers should not assume the animals are only a nighttime concern.A simple warning becomes a memorable road-safety messageWhat makes Japan's cat-warning signs particularly striking is the way they combine a serious safety message with an approachable visual style. Instead of presenting wildlife as an abstract road hazard, the signs put the animal itself at the centre of the warning. That can make drivers more likely to notice and remember the message, especially when the artwork is unusual enough to stand out from conventional road signage. But the signs should not be mistaken for evidence of a single nationwide programme requiring cat-warning signs on Japanese roads. They represent different local and organisational efforts, ranging from campaigns aimed at ordinary domestic cats to conservation measures protecting endangered wild cats. Together, they show how a simple roadside warning can be made more memorable while addressing a very real problem.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In the 1980s, Rutgers researcher Thomas Nosker mixed milk jugs with discarded Big Mac containers to make structural plastic lumber; about 1.5 million US rail ties have kept an estimated 300 million pounds of plastic out of landfills
articles.summary: US News: In an innovative breakthrough, Thomas Nosker, a Rutgers professor, created structural plastic lumber from milk jugs and Big Mac containers, resulting in 1.5 million railroad ties and diverting 300 million pounds of plastic waste from landfills.
articles.body: During the 1980s, Thomas Nosker was a doctoral student at Rutgers University who set out to address a mounting problem. It was the rapid accumulation of plastic packaging waste with no practical recycling pathway, according to a Rutgers Research profile of his work. Packaging materials such as plastic were rapidly replacing glass containers on store shelves, and the used bottles were piling up with no practical way to recycle them, so most of it was simply headed for landfills. This material was what Nosker eventually came up with after countless experiments and it is now called structural plastic lumber, a material that can replace wood and steel in their structural forms. Years later, that same material was used to manufacture roughly 1.5 million railroad ties across the United States, keeping an estimated 300 million pounds of plastic out of landfills, waterways and oceans.HDPE milk bottles were too cheap to recycleBottles manufactured using polyethylene terephthalate, called PET, could easily be sorted and processed for resale into items such as carpet or insulated clothing. High-density polyethylene, called HDPE, which is the plastic in milk jugs, was more problematic. As Nosker notes, the price of HDPE was so low that it didn't make economic sense to wash used milk jugs before recycling them on their own.Combining HDPE with polystyrene from Big Mac containersIt was during this time that the real breakthrough came, as Nosker began experimenting with blends rather than treating each plastic separately. He mixed HDPE with polystyrene salvaged from discarded Big Mac containers, the clamshell packaging McDonald's had used for its sandwiches before phasing it out beginning in the late 1980s and continuing into the early 1990s amid environmental pressure. Blending the two plastics sidestepped the economic problem entirely, since the finished composite drew its value from strength rather than the purity of either input material, meaning the low-value HDPE no longer needed to be washed or sorted on its own to be useful. Nosker found that certain blend ratios produced a much stronger material, likely because the particles of each plastic interlocked rather than separating.Proving plastic could replace woodConvincing an industry built entirely around wood lumber to accept a plastic substitute was never going to be easy; the material needed to prove its durability in the field, not just in a lab. As described in Rutgers's account of the invention, Nosker and his colleagues took a show-don't-tell approach, building actual structures rather than relying only on laboratory data, because wood had long been the default building material and skepticism toward a plastic alternative ran deep.In 2002, Nosker helped build New Jersey's first structural recycled-plastic bridge, a 40 to 42-foot vehicular span over the Mullica River in Wharton State Forest near Atsion Lake, in the Pine Barrens, an ecologically sensitive region where wood and steel structures typically degrade faster due to moisture and acidity in the soil. The accomplishment may have helped the material gain wider acceptance in the U.S. Army; in 2009, the Army demonstrated that a bridge built with the technology could carry a 73-ton M1 Abrams tank at Fort Bragg, North Carolina.1.5 million railway ties across the United StatesAmong other qualities of the final product, one should consider its density. As stated in Rutgers Research, the material is now used worldwide in bridges, railway ties, docks, and picnic tables, and has so far gone into roughly 1.5 million railway ties in the US. With each tie weighing approximately 200 pounds, Rutgers estimates that some 300 million pounds of plastic have been kept out of landfills and oceans as a result.Where the technology is used todayRutgers has since licensed the technology to two firms, AXION International Inc. of Zanesville, Ohio, and Sicut Enterprises Limited, based in London. According to Rutgers, both companies manufacture railroad ties and building materials from the recycled composite. In addition to railway ties, plastic lumber has found use on docks, picnic benches, park benches and parking bollards all over the U.S. and internationally. The Chicago Transit Authority has used the ties on its elevated tracks for track repair in an urban setting.Nosker holds more than 82 U.S. patents and pending patent applications related to plastic lumber and its manufacturing processes, according to Rutgers, work that has generated substantial licensing revenue for the university over the decades. He is currently working on the development of plastic composites reinforced by graphene for making light yet strong materials for use in vehicles and military applications. Even so, the plastic lumber project remains among Nosker's most visible contributions, a solution to a packaging waste problem that began with two of the most common items in American refrigerators and fast-food bags: a plastic milk jug and a foam sandwich box.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2024, a Chilean recycling manager deployed discarded salon hair in four booms and one mat in Laguna Verde; about a month later, the devices had reportedly trapped 15 kg of pollutants
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Discover how a unique project in Laguna Verde, Chile, utilizes discarded salon hair to create booms and mats that trap pollutants from greywater, showcasing an innovative approach to environmental conservation.
articles.body: In 2024, Mattia Carenini, who serves as the general manager of Matter of Trust Chile, used Petropelo hair booms in a stream located in Laguna Verde, which is a small town adjacent to Valparaíso, a coastal city. The greywater in the area contained oil and heavy metal pollutants from households and other businesses in the vicinity, and it was draining into the sea, thus providing an ideal scenario for testing a process that uses an extensively studied yet under-utilized property of hair, that is, its ability to soak up oil and heavy metals. In one month, as per the statement by Carenini, the booms collected 15 kg of pollutants from the water that flowed through them, according to El País, without independent verification from other sources.Turning salon sweepings into environmental toolsThe Matter of Trust Chile organization works in partnership with hairdressing salons and pet-grooming firms across the country in order to collect hair which, otherwise, would have been disposed of as garbage. This organization runs two main projects based on the use of the above-mentioned natural material, namely Petropelo, tube-shaped booms made of hair netting for trapping oil in lakes, rivers, and ocean waters, and Agropelo, hair mats used on agricultural land to reduce evaporation and save irrigation water. According to the description of the Laguna Verde project provided by Matter of Trust itself, the booms used here were made solely from salon and pet-groomer hair.Why hair works as an oil and metal absorbentThe science behind the technique rests on hair's composition. Human and animal hair is naturally oleophilic, meaning it attracts oil and hydrocarbons while resisting water absorption, which gives it a high capacity to remove pollutants from water without becoming waterlogged itself. The mesh booms installed at Laguna Verde were left in place for about a month, giving the hair enough time to absorb oil and heavy metals through direct contact with the greywater.A method already proven around the worldThis idea has already been tested in other cases. According to El País, in its description of the project, hair booms have been applied to solve the issue of oil spills throughout the world, such as the MV Wakashio oil spill, which occurred in 2020 due to the grounding of the ship off the shore of Mauritius, which is one of the notable cases where hair booms were applied. Matter of Trust, the U.S.-based nonprofit that launched the Chilean chapter, has worked on hair booms for many years.Part of what makes the Laguna Verde project notable is where the raw material comes from. As Luisiana Gil, a pet groomer from Santiago, put it, she was regularly throwing out bins full of her customers’ dog hair with nothing to do with them other than to throw them out at the dumpsite. The connection between the hair thrown out and the booms created by Matter of Trust Chile meant giving the useless hair a second life as an instrument of cleaning polluted water. Carenini has talked about their larger aim in the same incremental way, saying that the organization is restoring the site step by step.Scaling beyond a single streamThe organization believes that the amount of hair obtained from one person can be used to clean thousands of liters of water through the use of booms, which highlights the wastage of such absorbent materials in the form of hair that is considered worthless in many salons. Matter of Trust Chile, established in June 2020, is a nonprofit organization that has been identified by the Chilean government as an Institution of Public Interest. It continues to expand its network of partner salons. According to the organization's own site, its mission is to support farmers, fishers, and coastal communities in keeping water clean while regenerating soil.What the Laguna Verde result suggests going forwardBut while a 15-kilogram performance figure based only on one month’s effort at one location does not prove that hair booms can combat industrial-scale pollution, it does indicate that it is possible to see an effect from using a low-cost material made entirely out of waste produced in another industry. Whether the technique can scale up for larger or more polluted locations is still an open question and will probably depend upon the number of Chilean beauty and grooming salons that choose to donate their waste to Matter of Trust.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Since 2013, tourists have tossed coins into Japan’s Mount Fuji Oshino Hakkai ponds; about 50,000 were recovered amid concerns that corroding metal could affect the spring water
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Oshino Hakkai's beautiful spring-fed ponds at the foot of Mount Fuji have become unintended wishing wells, leading to the recovery of 50,000 coins. Local authorities warn of the potential environmental impact as they tackle the ongoing issue of coin tossing by tourists.
articles.body: One of Japan’s most recognisable water landscapes lies at the foot of Mount Fuji. Oshino Hakkai in Yamanashi Prefecture, consisting of eight spring-fed ponds, is celebrated for its clear water and its connection to the mountain’s underground springs. But in 2013, after Mount Fuji was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list, local authorities began confronting an unusual challenge: visitors were tossing coins into the ponds as if they were wishing wells. Over the years, around 50,000 coins have been recovered, raising concerns about the possible longer-term effects of corroding metal on the springs.The coin-tossing behaviour was not necessarily created by the 2013 World Heritage inscription, though. Instead, the site associates noted an increase in the practice alongside the surge in visitors after the mountain received its UNESCO status. Oshino Hakkai had already received national protection decades before the World Heritage listing, having been designated a national natural monument by the Japanese government back in 1934.The 2013 UNESCO listing covered a much larger cultural landscape called ‘Fujisan, sacred place and source of artistic inspiration.’ Comprising 25 components, the property is associated with Mount Fuji’s religious traditions and cultural influence, with Oshino Hakkai’s springs included among them.The ponds were never traditional wishing wellsOshino Hakkai’s eight ponds are associated with underground water which originates from Mount Fuji. Japan’s official tourism describes the site as a group of ponds fed by spring water and points out the notable clarity of Wakuike. An explanation from the Japanese government’s online magazine suggests that snow and rain falling on Mount Fuji can travel underground for more than 20 years before emerging as spring water around Oshino Hakkai.Wakuike, the best-known of the ponds, is sufficiently clear for travellers to see several metres into the water. The Japanese National Tourism Organisation notes that the pond’s spring water is considered one of the features that make the Oshino Hakkai a popular tourist destination near Mount Fuji.Meanwhile, the coin-tossing practice allegedly appears to have come from visitors rather than from a local tradition. According to The Independent, the village officials believe foreign tourists began tossing coins into the ponds, with the behaviour increasing after the 2013 UNESCO recognition. Recovered coins have included currencies from several countries, thus supporting the view that international tourism contributed substantially to the issue.While visitors who are accustomed to tossing coins into fountains or wishing wells might find this practice harmless, at Oshino Hakkai, the objects end up in natural spring water, which could cause trouble for the clear water in future. Therefore, the village has repeatedly asked people not to throw coins or other objects into any of the eight ponds and has warned that retrieving them is difficult.Thousands of coins have been removed from the pondsRepeated collection operations made the scale of the problem clear. In 2016, volunteer divers carried out five collection efforts at Wakuike and recovered more than 18,000 coins, demonstrating that coins were not simply a handful of isolated objects; instead, substantial amounts had accumulated on the pond floor.The low temperature and depth of the water reportedly make retrieving foreign objects particularly challenging. Furthermore, the repeated need for divers means that simply removing the coins does not provide a permanent solution if visitors continue the coin-tossing practice, adding new ones into the springs.Several reports say approximately 50,000 coins had been recovered from the ponds over the years through several operations. The environmental concern centres on the metals in the coins, as different coins contain different combinations of metals, and prolonged water exposure might cause corrosion. Village officials have expressed that continued accumulation and deterioration could eventually affect the pond environment. This is, however, a potential long-term risk and not evidence that the ponds have already suffered a documented contamination event caused by the coins.Warnings replaced the idea of a wishing wellAuthorities increasingly focused on prevention as the practice persisted. Warning signs have been displayed in multiple languages, including Japanese, English, Chinese and Korean, requesting visitors not to throw coins into the spring. Additionally, the village has also explored a way of accommodating visitors who want to make a monetary contribution without putting coins into the water. Most recently, Oshino Village has introduced an environmental-preservation contribution box project that aims to redirect such money toward maintaining the site’s environment. The village’s objective is to provide visitors with an alternative while also protecting the ponds from further deposits and reducing the need for repeated underwater diving operations.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Iran war energy costs hit US consumers at $1mn every 2 minutes: Report
articles.summary: US News: The Iran war has already cost US consumers more than $100 billion in higher gasoline and diesel prices, with the tab continuing to climb by roughly $1.
articles.body: The Iran war has already cost US consumers more than $100 billion in higher gasoline and diesel prices, with the tab continuing to climb by roughly $1 million every two minutes, according to a real-time estimate from Brown University’s Watson School.The cost works out to about $767 per US household since the conflict began on February 28, with gasoline accounting for roughly $55 billion and diesel for another $45.5 billion, according to Brown’s Iran War Energy Cost Tracker.The hit is getting heavier for diesel users as prices have risen about 61% from a year ago, reaching a record $5.90 a gallon on Monday, according to AAA. Diesel is heavily utilised in trucking, freight and travel, meaning higher fuel prices can feed into the price of goods and services across the economy.Texas has taken the biggest hit so far, with consumers paying about $11 billion more for gasoline and diesel since the war began, according to the tracker. California followed with about $8 billion and Florida with roughly $5 billion.Most of the household burden has come from gasoline, which rose from $2.98 a gallon when the war began to about $4.15, a 39% increase. The average household has spent an estimated $420 more on gasoline alone, according to Brown’s calculations.But diesel has become the bigger worry in recent weeks. Its price has climbed from $3.67 a gallon at the start of the war to $5.90, adding roughly $45.5 billion to the amount Americans have spent compared with the tracker’s no-war trajectory.The surge also creates a political problem for US President Donald Trump, who has argued that Americans are willing to bear higher prices to prevent Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon. But inflation remains voters’ top concern, and the president faces weak ratings on the issue.And there is little clarity yet on how much oil is continuing to leave the Middle East, a key factor in determining where fuel prices go from here. The war in Ukraine is adding another layer of pressure, with Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy infrastructure affecting global markets, particularly diesel.For American consumers, that could mean the $100 billion figure is far from the final bill. With less than two months before the midterm elections, the longer fuel prices remain elevated, the harder it could become for the administration to convince voters that the economic pain is worth the cost.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Virginia homeowner says Amazon's data centre turned his quiet life into 'chaos'; now he's suing over noise, flooding and damage
articles.summary: US News: Austin Newsom's quiet life in Louisa County, Virginia, changed after Amazon began building a huge data centre next to his property. Newsom lives with .
articles.body: Austin Newsom's quiet life in Louisa County, Virginia, changed after Amazon began building a huge data centre next to his property. Newsom lives with his wife in a three-bedroom house on Jefferson Highway. His boat repair and detailing business, Central VA Marine, also operates from the property. He says the construction has brought constant noise, flashing lights, dust, heavy machinery and traffic. He also says his water began turning brown, flooding appeared near his property and vibrations caused cracks in his home. Newsom filed a lawsuit against Amazon in August 2025. The case is now moving forward after a federal judge rejected Amazon's attempt to dismiss the main private-nuisance claim in July 2026.Amazon's Virginia project is being built beside his homeAmazon began construction of its Northeast Creek Technology Campus in March 2025. The development is planned across about 374 acres and includes 10 data-centre buildings, three substations, logistics and administrative buildings, stormwater facilities and other infrastructure. One Amazon property listed in the lawsuit at 2694 Jefferson Highway sits directly beside Newsom's home at 2623 Jefferson Highway. Construction is expected to continue until around 2031. The scale of the project has transformed the area around Newsom's property, which he says was once a quiet rural setting. He had also spent more than $80,000 renovating his house and planned to sell it after building another home nearby.Noise, lights, flooding and brown water are among his complaintsNewsom says the construction has brought extraordinarily loud noise to his property, including during hours restricted by Louisa County's noise rules. He also says flashing blue lights from the Amazon site shine almost continuously and are visible from his home at night. Another major complaint concerns his water supply. According to the lawsuit, his water began intermittently turning brown soon after construction started. Newsom says he had never experienced the problem before and became reluctant to drink the water. The lawsuit also alleges that excavation changed natural drainage patterns and contributed to flooding near his property. Dust and debris from construction have added to the disruption, while Newsom says vibrations from heavy machinery have caused cracks in his house.The disruption is affecting his boat repair business and propertyNewsom's home is also the base for Central VA Marine, the boat repair and detailing business he co-owns. The lawsuit says construction has created heavy traffic, road damage, dust and safety problems around the business. Newsom says some customers have struggled to access the property with boats and that some have said they will not return until the construction ends. He also says the project has made it harder to sell his home. Realtor.com reported that a local real-estate agent described the property as difficult to market because the construction is so visible. Newsom had planned to sell the house after completing another home nearby, but says the construction has undermined those plans and reduced the property's appeal.Federal judge allows the nuisance lawsuit to continueNewsom and Central VA Marine filed their lawsuit in Louisa County Circuit Court on August 11, 2025. Amazon moved the case to federal court and later asked for the claims to be dismissed. On July 10, 2026, US District Judge Jasmine H. Yoon allowed the main private-nuisance claim to proceed. The judge considered the combined allegations of noise, dust, debris, flashing lights, vibrations, structural cracking, flooding and water problems and found that they were sufficient to plead a potentially substantial and unreasonable interference with the property. The judge dismissed a separate claim seeking temporary injunctive relief because an injunction is a remedy rather than an independent cause of action. The ruling did not end Newsom's ability to seek injunctive relief as part of the surviving nuisance case.His fight reflects a bigger conflict over data-centre growthNewsom's dispute comes as Virginia sees rapid growth in data-centre construction driven by cloud computing and artificial intelligence. Amazon is developing another data-centre campus in Louisa County, while a third proposed project was withdrawn in July 2025 following opposition from local residents. Newsom has also raised concerns about a proposed transmission project that would serve the region's growing electricity demand from data centres. He told Realtor.com that the proposed power line could affect his property as well.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2001, architect James Corner won the plan to cap 150 million tonnes of New York rubbish; Freshkills is becoming a 2,315-acre park with restored forests
articles.summary: US News: Discover how Freshkills, once New York City's largest landfill, is transforming into a massive 2,315-acre park featuring restored ecosystems, trails, and recreational areas.
articles.body: New York City announced the international design competition for Fresh Kills Park in 2001, when the site was still closely associated with its previous role as the city's enormous garbage dump. Fresh Kills had operated on Staten Island since 1948, and contained roughly 150 million tons of garbage by the time it stopped receiving household waste.The winning proposal came from landscape architecture firm Field Operations, led by James Corner. The city's Freshkills Park timeline records December 18, 2001, as the date Field Operations won the design competition. The site had to be capped, monitored and engineered while its landscape was gradually rebuilt around the existing landfill infrastructure.The original plan covered 2,315 acresThe Draft Master Plan described Fresh Kills as a 2,315-acre site, which is nearly three times the size of Central Park. Its proposal included converting the former landfill into a large public landscape that contained tidal marshes, creeks, trails, recreational areas and wildlife habitat. The plan divided the property into five major landscape areas and treated the transformation as a process that would unfold over decades.The scale of the project was partly determined by the landfill itself, and the enormous mounds could not simply be excavated and removed. Instead, the waste would remain underground beneath engineered layers that were designed to isolate it from the surrounding environment. The park's eventual landscape would therefore sit partly on top of a massive waste system.James Corner's plan turned a closed landfill into a landscapeNew York City launched the international design competition for Fresh Kills Park on September 5, 2001, as officials prepared for the landfill's final closure and considered how the enormous Staten Island site could eventually be reused. Three months later, on December 18, the city selected Field Operations, the landscape architecture firm led by James Corner, as the competition winner. Corner's team envisioned a large public landscape built over the capped landfill, with restored wetlands, forests, grasslands, waterways, trails and areas for recreation. The design also worked with the landfill's existing topography, turning the massive waste mounds into rolling hills that would become part of the future park. According to the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation's Fresh Kills project history, the competition was followed by master planning and public outreach beginning in 2003, while the city's draft master plan described the site as a 2,315-acre landscape containing about 150 million tons of residential waste. The project therefore required more than landscape design, since the landfill had to be capped and monitored before large sections could safely support the forests, wetlands and public spaces that were envisioned in Corner's winning proposal.The landfill's engineering remains underneathThe city's master plan described the landfill as a highly engineered landscape, and sections of the site were covered with layers designed to contain the waste and manage water and landfill gases. That infrastructure remains part of Freshkills' long-term operation.The park's landscape was therefore designed around the realities of the landfill rather than treating those realities as something that could be erased. The large mounds that eventually became grassy hills and viewpoints were created by decades of waste disposal, while drainage systems, landfill-gas infrastructure and monitoring remain necessary beneath the park.Parts of the park are already openFreshkills Park is now generally described by its current management as a 2,200-acre landfill-to-park project, and is being developed in phases, with the edges of the site opening before the interior areas. Schmul Park was redesigned in 2012, while Owl Hollow Soccer Fields opened in 2013, and the New Springville Greenway opened in 2015.North Park Phase 1 opened in 2023, and includes paths for walking and biking, a bird observation tower, a wetland overlook and newly planted vegetation. Visitors can look across Main Creek and the restored wetlands from the park's elevated areas. Most of Freshkills remains closed outside scheduled tours and events because the larger transformation is still underway.A park built around what could not be removedThe waste that created the landfill has not disappeared; instead, the city has spent decades engineering the site so that a new landscape can exist above and around it. The original plan called for more than 40 miles of trails and pathways across the 2,315-acre site, and also proposed extensive ecological restoration.Some of those plans have changed as the project has moved from design to construction, and the park is now described as 2,200 acres. The hills, wetlands and forests that are taking shape on Staten Island are being built around the infrastructure that still contains the city's former garbage dump.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2017, a Texas State University dye-tracing study followed fluorescein from the Pedernales River to a spring; the dye was detected 2.4 miles away in about 15.5 hours
articles.summary: US News: In a groundbreaking experiment, researchers in Texas used fluorescein dye to trace the flow of water from the Pedernales River to the spring at Pedernales Falls State Park, revealing a hidden underground connection and shedding light on river behavior.
articles.body: A river can sometimes seem to disappear without actually going anywhere. Underneath the hard, rocky surface of Texas Hill Country, water may seep into the gaps, crevices, and underground passages and come back to the surface some distance away. In 2017, researchers used a bright green fluorescent dye to demonstrate how this process occurs in the Pedernales River to connect the river with the spring of Pedernales Falls State Park.According to a 2017 technical report by The Meadows Centre for Water and the Environment at Texas State University, streamflow gain-and-loss studies had shown that the Pedernales River was generally a gaining stream. Still, the 2016 survey identified a losing reach upstream of Pedernales Falls State Park, followed by significant gains downstream. The findings suggested that water was leaving the river through underground recharge features before returning further downstream. Earlier work by geologist Gunnar Brune, along with observations from long-time residents, had pointed to a swallet, or sink, near the remains of the old Robinson ranch house as the likely point where river water entered the subsurface. The 2017 dye-tracing experiment subsequently confirmed that this underground diversion of river water mainly supplied the spring at the base of the falls.Following water into the darkFor the purpose of testing the hypothesis, scientists working at The Meadows Centre for Water and the Environment, along with partnering organisations, took advantage of one of the most important methods of hydrogeology, which is the process of dye tracing. On August 21, 2017, the scientists combined three pounds of a powdered form of fluorescein dye that contained 75% dye by weight and mixed it with the river water. This combination was released into the Pedernales stream above the suspected losing feature around 3 pm. Research had already been carried out in this area for one week before the experiment took place. It is critical to note that natural substances, particulate matter and even man-made substances have the capability of giving off fluorescence that might end up being misidentified as the tracer.The charcoal samplers were set in place while the field fluorimeter was set up by the spring. This technique is widely used in karst and fractured-rock environments because fluorescent dyes can reveal underground connections that are difficult to map from the surface. Research published in Hydrogeology Journal describes dye tracing as a classic hydrogeological technique for investigating surface-water and groundwater flow, including underground flow paths and water-transit times in karst systems. In the Pedernales experiment, the dye behaved as researchers expected. After being released, fluorescein dye was observed in the spring after it was injected into the river, indicating a hydraulic link between the two bodies of water. The 2017 Texas State University Meadows Centre technical report documented the result in about 15.5 hours.A hidden shortcut beneath the riverAs noted by the Meadows Centre for Water and the Environment, the suspected swallet and the spring were about 2.4 miles apart, providing strong evidence that river water reached the spring through the subsurface. This discovery not only provided an answer to why a certain phenomenon occurred but also shed light on the reasons for another seemingly inexplicable characteristic of the river. Instead of being absorbed into the ground, some of the water from the Pedernales was undergoing an underground journey. That geological setting also plays a significant role, as the Marble Falls Formation contains fractures and openings capable of allowing water to move underground. The study report notes that the spring's source was mainly a diversion of river water through the swallet, rather than an entirely separate groundwater source. The travel time was also informative. By dividing 2.4 miles by 15.5 hours, we get 0.15 miles per hour, or 250 meters per hour. It does not measure the speed through every underground conduit, because the measured distance is between the injection point and the detector, not the actual route the water took. However, it shows how fast water travels through underground conduits.Why a disappearing river mattersThe Pedernales River is not just a beautiful stream flowing through the Hill Country area. The river flows for more than 100 miles into the Colorado River and contributes to Lake Travis, a major water source in the region. The river's behaviour is closely tied to the springs and groundwater system beneath the surrounding land. The study conducted in 2017 is not just an example of a geological phenomenon. The experiment can help identify areas where groundwater and surface water are directly connected. This is especially helpful during drought because, at times, the river and the aquifer beneath it can be closely linked. Sometimes a losing stretch of river can feed another stretch through springs.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2011, marine scientist Nick Hill helped launch a programme turning abandoned fishing nets into carpet yarn; 300 tonnes recycled and other conservation efforts helped protect 5,700 hectares of ocean
articles.summary: Rest of World News: For a long time, coastal communities in the central Philippines have balanced two sources of income. There are risks associated with either sending bo.
articles.body: For a long time, coastal communities in the central Philippines have balanced two sources of income. There are risks associated with either sending boats out to fish or tending rows of seaweed lines stretched over shallow lagoons. Seasonal variations in fish catches and global demand for seaweed can cause a household to run out of food or money during a challenging year. A young marine researcher was initially drawn to the area by this daily balancing act that took place in dozens of small island settlements, and it ultimately resulted in one of the more peculiar fishing net recycling stories in contemporary ocean conservation.A scientist's discovery in the waterIn 2006, Nick Hill was working on his PhD at the Institute of Zoology in London, studying how access to capital and food security affected whether coastal people in the central Philippines decided to fish or produce seaweed instead. His fieldwork was part of conservation work that the Zoological Society of London had already been doing with Project Seahorse, work that had helped build more than thirty community-managed marine protected areas around the region. Those reserves were paying off, but they still needed consistent funding and ongoing community support to survive from year to year. Hill and his colleagues began searching for a new source of income that would help make local conservation efforts financially sustainable, without depending solely on grant funding.Looks like the missing piece was on the seabed all along. Fishing boats were throwing out nets that trapped marine species and fouled reefs. Made from nylon, the nets might remain in seawater for centuries, polluting the waterways that the new reserves were designed to safeguard. Hill’s team began to wonder if the Philippine nets might be a resource that paid for themselves, rather than waste to be carted away and forgotten.A partnership nobody expectedBy 2011, the American flooring manufacturer Interface was already collaborating with the Italian firm Aquafil, a business that had pioneered a means of regenerating nylon yarn from old fishing gear and other industrial waste that it offers as ECONYL, so there was a solution to that concern. The interface supplied startup funds and business strategy, Aquafil converted the baled nylon into new yarn, and a community banking system drawn from development finance enabled families to save and trade against future net collections. The three partners believed that a cooperative program might satisfy both conservation goals and household incomes, as the group had developed community links in the region since 1996.The ensuing operation was named Net Works, and people were instructed to gather, clean and bale old nets instead of letting them pile up on the shoreline or lie stranded on reefs. The interface supplied startup funds and business strategy; Aquafil converted the baled nylon into new yarn, and a community banking system drawn from development finance enabled families to save and trade against future net collections. The torn net, once a mere hazard for villagers, is now sold into a supply chain that feeds carpet manufacturing on the other side of the world.From pilot project to global ocean conservation enterpriseAccording to ZSL, the programme has recycled some 270 million metres of fishing net and 300 tonnes of disused gear across 32 villages, while also helping to expand and improve the management of local marine protected areas. Then the identical net for the cash model was tested in Cameroon and Indonesia, adapting the approach to different coastlines and fishing cultures. That success eventually led the programme to outgrow its identity as a single conservation project and to split off as an independent social company. That enterprise, Coast4C, now organises its work around communities, commerce, conservation and climate and has so far protected more than 5,700 hectares of ocean while supporting over 2,000 households through 86 community banks.Separate reporting on the wider ghost net recycling movement by National Geographic has described how such models connect marginalised coastal communities directly to mainstream global supply chains, turning ghost gear into both income and habitat protection. Today, the program is led by Hill, alongside Amado Blanco, who helped develop the original version of the scheme on the ground in the Philippines back in 2011. What started as a doctorate topic regarding fishing livelihoods has become a model other conservation groups are now studying as they consider how to finance reef protection without relying solely on contributions. Once a threat to Philippine reefs, nets are now more likely to be underfoot, woven into carpet tiles thousands of kilometres from the waters they came from.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
